The `sha512sums` array includes a valid checksum for the source tarball and marks the signature file with 'SKIP', which is acceptable for this audit phase since verification occurs later and does not affect the safety of source extraction. There is no code in the global scope or in `pkgver()` that performs dangerous operations such as executing downloaded content, making unauthorized network requests, or exfiltrating data. The `pkgver` is hardcoded, so no dynamic version fetching occurs. The top-level logic consists only of static variable assignments, which are safe. Therefore, running `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo` will safely download and parse the sources without executing any malicious code.
</details>

The `.SRCINFO` file defines metadata for the `apparmor.d-base` package and related subpackages. It specifies the source as a tagged release tarball from the official GitHub repository (https://github.com/roddhjav/apparmor.d), along with a PGP signature for verification. The `validpgpkeys` array includes the maintainer's key fingerprint, which is a standard and secure practice for verifying authenticity. While one of the `sha512sums` is marked as `SKIP` (for the `.asc` file), this is common and acceptable when the file is verified via PGP, as the cryptographic signature provides stronger assurance than a checksum.

The package depends only on AppArmor and related components, which aligns with its purpose of providing AppArmor profiles. No network operations, file modifications, or executable logic are present in this file — it is purely declarative metadata used by Arch Linux packaging tools. There are no signs of obfuscated commands, unexpected downloads, or malicious behavior. The use of standard AUR practices (e.g., VCS release sources, PGP verification) further supports the legitimacy of this package.

All elements in the file are consistent with normal, safe AUR packaging workflows. The presence of `SKIP` for the signature file's checksum does not weaken security, as the signature itself is verified against a trusted key. No evidence of supply-chain tampering or malicious intent is found.
</details>

<security_assessment>

<details>
The PKGBUILD file defines a package for `apparmor.d`, which provides AppArmor profiles and tools. It fetches a source tarball and an associated PGP signature from the project's official GitHub release page (`https://github.com/roddhjav/apparmor.d`). The source integrity is partially verified via a `sha512sums` entry for the tarball and a `SKIP` for the signature — while the signature is not verified due to `SKIP`, the use of a PGP signature and declared `validpgpkeys` is a standard AUR practice, especially when verification might be handled externally or in a build environment with the key pre-imported.

The build process uses standard environment variables and invokes `just`, a common build automation tool, to run `prebuild` and installation targets. All operations are confined to the build directory and package directory (`$pkgdir`), with no evidence of unauthorized network access, obfuscated code, or suspicious file operations. The dependencies and build tools (`go`, `git`, `just`) are appropriate for the project type.

There are no dangerous commands (e.g., `eval`, `curl|bash`, `base64` decoding), no data exfiltration attempts, and no execution of externally fetched code. The maintainer includes a comment about their public key, which is benign. The package follows standard AUR packaging practices and poses no evident supply-chain risk.
</details>
